entries.name: Seollal
entries.capsule: Korean Lunar New Year: family rites, bowing to elders, tteokguk soup; Minnesota groups hold a public celebration each winter.
entries.dateRule: First day of the first month of the Korean lunisolar calendar. In South Korea the holiday spans the day before through the day after.

dates.source: Sahan Journal (Year of the Fire Horse began Feb. 17); PublicHolidays.co.kr lists Feb. 16-18 holiday
PublicHolidays.co.kr (estimate for this year); also seed calculation
Seed calculation; PublicHolidays.co.kr estimates Jan. 26-27

entries.whatItMarks: Start of the lunisolar year. Sources describe tteokguk (rice cake soup) and saebae, bowing to elders.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: A public Seollal celebration with JangmiArts is held each winter in the White Bear Lake area: Feb. 10, 2024 and Feb. 1, 2025 at White Bear Lake High School (CBS named the Korean American Association of Minnesota as co-host; Sahan Journal named the Korean Cultural Association in 2025), and Feb. 21, 2026 at Mariner Middle School with a marketplace, dance and dessert reception. Sejong Academy students hold a Korean New Year program with drumming, saebae and a hanbok walk. AK Connection mentions an annual Seollal gathering for adoptees.

entries.name: Chuseok
entries.capsule: Korean harvest festival honoring ancestors; in Minnesota, AK Connection holds a free public Chuseok Festival.
entries.dateRule: Fifteenth day of the eighth month of the Korean lunisolar calendar; the South Korean holiday spans three days.

entries.whatItMarks: Autumn harvest and ancestral remembrance; families gather and set a table for ancestors.
entries.howCelebratedInMinnesota: AK Connection's Chuseok Festival, Sept. 26, 2026, 4 to 10 p.m., East Side Neighborhood Services, Minneapolis: free, with a sensory-friendly hour, Korean market, food, noraebang and performances. Adoptee Hub timed its 2024 Kimchi Festival (Sept. 29, 2024, Wolfe Park, St. Louis Park) to Chuseok.
